/-!
# Erdős Problem 914

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/914](https://www.erdosproblems.com/914)
- [CoHa63] Corrádi, K. and Hajnal, A., *On the maximal number of independent circuits in a graph*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1963), 423-439.
- [HaSz70] Hajnal, A. and Szemerédi, E., *Proof of a conjecture of P. Erdős*. (1970), 601-623.
- [KiKo08] Kierstead, H. A. and Kostochka, A. V., *A short proof of the Hajnal-Szemerédi theorem on
  equitable colouring*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2008), 265-270.
-/

namespace Erdos914

/--
Let $r\geq 2$ and $m\geq 1$. Every graph with $rm$ vertices and minimum degree at least $m(r-1)$
contains $m$ vertex disjoint copies of $K_r$.

When $r=2$ this follows from Dirac's theorem. Corrádi and Hajnal [CoHa63] proved this when $r=3$.
Hajnal and Szemerédi [HaSz70] proved this for all $r\geq 4$.

A shorter proof was given by Kierstead and Kostochka [KiKo08].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos914.lean"]
theorem erdos_914 {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m)
    (hdeg : m * (r - 1) ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ K : Fin m → Finset V, (∀ i, G.IsNClique r (K i)) ∧
      Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (K i) (K j) := by
  sorry

/--
Equivalently, every graph with $rm$ vertices and maximum degree at most $m-1$ has a proper vertex
colouring with $m$ colours in which every colour class has exactly $r$ vertices (an equitable
colouring).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*}
    [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m)
    (hdeg : G.maxDegree ≤ m - 1) :
    ∃ C : G.Coloring (Fin m), ∀ i, (C.colorClass i).ncard = r := by
  sorry

end Erdos914

reformulations.difference: States the complementary proper-colouring version of the clique-packing problem, and requires every colour class to have exactly r vertices rather than merely requiring class sizes to differ by at most one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n = r*m > 0, complementation changes the minimum-degree bound m*(r-1) into the maximum-degree bound m-1, since complementary vertex degrees sum to n-1. Colour classes of a proper colouring are cliques in the complement. Conversely, m pairwise disjoint r-cliques cover all r*m vertices, so labelling them gives a proper colouring of the complement. Finally, m integer class sizes summing to r*m and differing by at most one must all equal r. These degree, covering, packing/colouring, and equal-class/equitable equivalences were proved in the scratch file without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems.

sources_consulted: Kierstead–Kostochka (2008), A Short Proof of the Hajnal–Szemerédi Theorem on Equitable Colouring: publisher abstract and references, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548307008619
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equitable_coloring (definition, Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem, historical remarks and references)

review.notes: Both declarations were checked, including quantifiers, degree bounds, exact clique cardinalities, disjointness, and finite colour-class cardinalities. The hypotheses force at least two vertices, so empty-graph degree defaults cannot affect either statement; all colour classes are finite, so ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and its equivalence lemmas use only standard axioms. Boundary tests included r=2,m=1 and sharp-bound multipartite examples for (r,m)=(2,2),(3,1),(3,2),(4,2). The linked proof's final theorem implies the repository statement and contains no sorry or custom axiom declarations; it was inspected, not rebuilt against its older Lean toolchain. Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/914 and its forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The precise cited Kierstead–Kostochka abstract provided an independent mathematical statement for comparison. Full texts of the older historical references were unavailable; their bibliographic details and attributions were corroborated through the accessible sources.
